content:
alex: Heads-up: hitting two linked issues in Ruby SDK when using function/tool calling over streaming: (1) streaming chunks sometimes cut JSON tokens so parser fails; (2) retries/auth refresh can cause duplicate tool invocations. Anyone seen this?

kim: yep saw similar. Which model/endpoint? Are you using `client.stream_tool_call` or our low-level stream?

alex: Using hosted infer and our `ruby-client` helper `stream_tool_call`. Repro: nested object with optional int field sometimes arrives as the JSON string "123" (number encoded as string) or split across chunks like '"12' and '"3"'. Parser raises JSON::ParserError and our funccall schema validator rejects.

riya: ugh. Streaming chunk boundaries are terrible. Two ideas: (A) buffer+incremental-parse with tolerant fallback (try to append next chunk before failing), (B) coerce simple scalar types in validator with permissive rules. We implemented a small helper in Python; can port to Ruby.

kim: ```
buffer = ""
stream.each do |chunk|
  buffer << chunk
  begin
    obj = JSON.parse(buffer)
    handle(obj)
    buffer = ""
  rescue JSON::ParserError
    # wait for more chunks
    next
  end
end
```

alex: That helps for chunking but not for coerced types. Also need to avoid double-invoke when retry happens: we see control flow retrying the request at HTTP layer, but tools are invoked client-side as a side-effect when the parsed func call is returned. Maybe make tool invocation idempotent or attach a request-id?

riya: We added `idempotency_key` for tool calls and server keeps last-seen keys for ~10s. For hosted mode can't rely on that for private customers. Alternative: client should not execute tool until finalization ack from response end. For streaming, emit 'candidate func-call' events but only run on `end_of_stream` unless you set `eager_execute: true`.

alex: Interesting — can we add `eager_execute: :best_effort` with safety: if retry occurs, SDK will de-dupe via local cache of request IDs. Proposal: SDK helper `stream_func_call_safe` that buffers partial JSON, incrementally validates with permissive coercion, emits `on_candidate`, and only calls tool on `on_commit`. Thoughts?

kim: Yes please. Also add `coerce_to_types` option mapping schema paths to lambdas. e.g., { 'params.age' => lambda{|v| v.to_i rescue v} }. We should write tests for split-quotes and token-refresh simulation.

riya: ```
client.stream_func_call_safe(
  request,
  coerce_map: { "params.age" => ->(v){ v.to_i rescue nil } },
  idempotency_key: SecureRandom.uuid,
  on_candidate: ->(obj){ puts "preview: #{obj}" },
  on_commit: ->(obj){ tool_runner.call(obj) }
)
```

alex: I'll open a PR with tests and add a comment to review: @kim @riya. CI bot: can you run the flaky stream test locally? :pray:

ci-bot: CI: started run 4928 for branch alex/ruby-stream-safe. Status: queued

kim: Thanks. Also note tokens refresh race — we'll add a hook to pause streaming while refresh in-flight. Small edge but saved us.

alex: Cool. PR in ~1h. marking as blocked -> not blocked. :thumbsup:
